chunks: 4733 - And in the narration of Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith—We will join their descendants with them."
He said: "The children fell short of the deeds of the fathers, so Allah joined the children with the fathers so that their eyes might be comforted by that."

key_terms.آمَنُوا: believed; referring to those possessing iman
key_terms.أَعْيُنُهُمْ: their eyes; meaning their joy and comfort
key_terms.أَلْحَقْنَا: We joined or caused to follow
key_terms.بِإِيمَانٍ: with faith; the condition of believing adherence

ai.seo_question: How does Allah reunite believing children with their parents in the hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that Allah joins believing descendants to their believing forefathers even when the children have not reached the same level of deeds. The verse highlights Allah’s mercy toward believing families and the joy granted to them through reunion. It indicates a gracious divine favor connected to iman and family attachment in the hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4733 - In the narration of Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, Abu Abdullah (as) said regarding the words of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic:
"And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith - We will join them with their descendants" (Surah At-Tur 52:21),
Imam (as) said: "The children fell short of the deeds of their fathers, so Allah (swt) joined the children with their fathers to bring comfort to their eyes."
